title.en: How hyaluronic acid filler works for your chin

intro.en: Hyaluronic acid (HA) filler is a smooth, cross-linked gel. For the chin, we use a firm HA with strong lift, placed close to the chin bone, where it adds structure and shape right away. Most HA fillers contain lidocaine for comfort, and HA can be dissolved if needed.

text.en: A firm gel placed over the chin bone brings a recessed chin forward, so the lower face looks stronger and better supported.
From the side, the tip of the nose, the lips and the chin come into line, so the nose looks in proportion and the lips sit in balance.
Small amounts shape the chin softer and rounder, or more defined, to suit your features and your style.
Where needed, we blend the chin into the jaw for one clean line from chin to ear, so it never looks added on.

note.en: Hyaluronic acid fillers are FDA-approved. We’ll tell you which product we recommend for you, and why.

text.en: Cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA), a water-holding sugar your body already makes. For the chin we use a firm HA (high G′) that holds its shape over the bone. It contains lidocaine and can be dissolved if needed.
We read your whole profile first, then place filler precisely so the chin looks natural at rest and when you smile. Results soften gradually over time.

q.en: Does it hurt? Any side effects?

a.en:
We apply a numbing cream first, and most fillers also contain a local anesthetic. Most clients feel only light pressure.

Swelling, bruising, redness or tenderness are common and usually settle within a few days to a week. Less often: small lumps or unevenness, which can usually be corrected. Rarely, filler can block a blood vessel. This needs immediate care, so call us right away if you notice unusual pain, skin color changes or any change in your vision.

q.en: Will it look natural?

a.en: Yes. We plan your chin around your whole profile, not a template, and build gradually. Hyaluronic acid filler can be dissolved if needed.

q.en: Who should not have it?

a.en: It is not suitable during pregnancy or breastfeeding, if you have an active skin infection or cold sore in the area, or if you have a history of severe allergies to filler ingredients. Talk to us first about bleeding disorders, autoimmune conditions or recent procedures in the area.

q.en: What should I know before and after?

a.en:
Before: For 7 days, avoid alcohol and supplements that can increase bruising, such as fish oil, vitamin E and ibuprofen, unless they are prescribed for you. Plan at least 2 weeks before a big event. Come in with clean, makeup-free skin.

After: Mild swelling, tenderness or bruising is normal for a few days. Use a cold compress as needed. Skip intense workouts, saunas and alcohol for 24–48 hours. Don’t press or massage the area unless we ask you to.

q.en: When will I see results?

a.en: You’ll see the change right away. The final result settles in about 2 weeks. How long it lasts depends on the product and your body. Results vary by individual. We see you for a check-in at about 2 weeks, then maintenance as the filler gradually softens.

Both are FDA-approved wrinkle relaxers that soften expression lines. So why do clinics offer two? Here is what our providers tell clients in consultation.
What’s the difference?
Botox® contains the active ingredient plus accessory proteins. Xeomin® is purified to the active ingredient alone, which is why it is sometimes called a “naked” formula.
For most people, results look the same. Placement and dose matter far more than the brand.
What’s the same
Both start working in about 3–5 days, reach full effect around day 14, and last about 3–4 months.
How we choose
We consider your history with each product, your goals and your budget. Your provider explains the options and gives you a clear quote at consultation.
What to expect
Treatment takes 10–20 minutes with no downtime. Stay upright for 4 hours and skip workouts for 24 hours.
The bottom line
Choose a provider, not a brand. A good plan uses the right product in the right places.
